originalTitle: Global Market:  China stocks hold steady despite GDP miss as investors shift to consumer, financial shares
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: Chinese stocks didn't go down much even though the country's economic growth wasn't as good as expected. This is because investors started paying more attention to companies that make everyday products and financial services, rather than just technology companies. As a result, stocks in these areas went up, while technology stocks went down a bit. The stock market in Hong Kong did better than the one in mainland China, thanks to big tech companies. Overall, investors from Europe are still very interested in buying Chinese stocks, which is helping to support the market.

originalTitle: Groww Q1 Results: Net profit spikes 94% YoY to Rs 735 crore; revenue jumps 66%
simplifiedContent: Groww, a company that helps people invest in the stock market, just released its quarterly results. The company made a net profit of Rs 735 crore, which is 94% more than it made during the same time last year. Its revenue, or the money it made from its main business, also increased by 66% to Rs 1,504 crore. This means the company is doing better than it was last year, which is a positive sign. The company's profit also increased by 7% from the previous quarter, showing continued growth.

originalTitle: Kusumgar shares jump 10% after solid D-Street debut. What investors should do now?
simplifiedContent: Kusumgar shares had a strong first day on the stock market, starting 37% higher than their initial price and continuing to rise. This is a good sign for the company, which makes special fabrics and supplies the defense industry. Even though analysts think the company will do well in the long run, they suggest that investors sell some of their shares to make a profit and hold on to the rest with a plan to sell if the price falls. This is because the shares have already gone up a lot and it's a good idea to be cautious. The company's successful start on the stock market and positive analyst views are why the shares jumped 10% initially.

originalTitle: Laser Power IPO listing tomorrow: Here’s what GMP hints ahead of debut
simplifiedContent: The company Laser Power & Infra is going to start trading on the Indian stock market tomorrow, July 16. Before its launch, people were able to buy its shares at a price between ₹203 and ₹214. Many big investors, like QIBs and NIIs, showed a lot of interest in buying these shares. Now, people think the shares will be worth around ₹258 when they start trading, which is about 20.56% more than the original price. This could be a good sign for the company's first day on the market.

originalTitle: Groww Q1 results: Net profit jumps 94% to  ₹735 crore, revenue grows 66% YoY
simplifiedContent: Groww, a company, has just released its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company made a net profit of ₹735 crore, which is 94% more than what it made during the same time last year. The company's revenue also grew by 66% compared to last year. This means that Groww is making more money and growing faster than it was before. This is a positive sign for the company and its investors, as it suggests that the company is doing well and may continue to grow in the future.

originalTitle: Caliber Mining & Logistics IPO: GMP signals modest listing gains; 10 key things to know from RHP
simplifiedContent: Caliber Mining is having an Initial Public Offering (IPO), which means it's selling shares to the public for the first time. The company is selling 94 lakh new shares and some existing shareholders are selling 12 lakh of their shares. The IPO will be open for people to buy shares from July 17 to July 21. This is a "book build issue", which is a way of selling shares where the price is decided based on demand. The IPO is expected to have modest gains when it lists on the stock market, according to GMP (a financial advisor), which might be interesting for people thinking of investing.
